title: Viterbi Decoding and MEMMs
oneLiner: Find the best sequence of tags quickly by keeping only the best route into each tag, then upgrade the tagger to use any clue you like.

what.html:
The Viterbi algorithm finds the most likely tag sequence without trying every possibility: word by word, it keeps just the best-scoring path into each tag and a pointer to where that path came from. A MEMM is a smarter tagger that predicts each tag from many clues (spelling, neighbours) with logistic regression, and is decoded the same way.

Everyday versionPlanning the cheapest road trip through several cities, you only remember the cheapest way to reach each city so far. You never need the full list of every possible route.

why.html:
• Trying all tag sequences is impossible (billions for a short sentence); Viterbi is fast.
  • The same trick runs inside speech recognisers, name finders and modern taggers.
  • Feature-based taggers fix many weaknesses of counting-only HMMs.

how.title: The goal
how.html: We know the words; we want the hidden tags with the highest overall probability. With 45 tags, ten words have 3.4 × 10¹⁶ possible tag sequences, so we need a shortcut.

how.title: One cell at a time
how.html: For each tag at each word: try each tag at the previous word, multiply by the transition, keep the best, multiply by the chance of the word. Previous Verb 0.03 × 0.2 = 0.006 beats Noun 0.0015 × 0.3, so the pointer goes to Verb.

how.title: A whole sentence
how.html: Fill the table for "the doctor is in" column by column, then follow the pointers back from the best last cell: Det, Noun, Verb, Prep.

how.title: Hot or cold?
how.html: Three ice creams then one: day 1 hot (0.32), day 2 cold (0.064) beats hot (0.0384). Best story: hot, then cold.

how.title: Fast, but the model is limited
how.html: Viterbi's work grows with (tags)² × words. The HMM itself struggles with unseen words, can't use spelling clues, and only looks backward.

how.title: Any clue as a feature
how.html: A MEMM scores each tag from features like "previous tag is a modal" or "word ends in -ck", then softmax turns scores into probabilities: scores 2.0 and 0.5 become 82% and 18%.

how.title: Don't decide too early
how.html: Picking the best tag word by word can trap you: "the old man the boats" needs "old" as a noun and "man" as a verb. Viterbi finds it; greedy doesn't. MEMMs also have a quirk (label bias) that CRFs fix.

demo.html: Sort each statement: is it about the counting-based HMM, the feature-based MEMM, or both?

example.html:
The last column of "the doctor is in". "is" as a verb scored 0.027216. For "in" as a preposition: 0.027216 × 0.2 (verb → preposition) × 1.0 = 0.005443, the best final score, so we trace back Prep ← Verb ← Noun ← Det.

Supplementary Swap "max" for "sum" in Viterbi and you get the forward algorithm, which gives the total probability of the words over all tag paths.

misunderstandings: Viterbi picks each word's best tag.
It picks the best whole path.
It's exact for HMMs (beam search is the approximation).
takeaways: Decoding = argmax tag sequence; brute force is Nⁿ.
the doctor is in → Det Noun Verb Prep (0.005443).
O(N²T); HMMs limited by unknown words, features, context.
MEMM = per-word logistic regression; Viterbi beats greedy; label bias → CRF.
thirty: Decoding finds argmax P(t | w) = argmax Π P(tᵢ|tᵢ₋₁)P(wᵢ|tᵢ); brute force costs Nⁿ. Viterbi keeps vₜ(j) = maxᵢ vₜ₋₁(i)aᵢⱼbⱼ(oₜ) plus backpointers, then backtraces (one cell: 0.03 × 0.2 = 0.006 beats 0.0015 × 0.3). 'the doctor is in': Det 0.21; Noun 0.0756, Verb 0.00021; is/Verb 0.027216, is/Noun 0.001512; in/Prep 0.005443, in/Adv 0.000272 → Det Noun Verb Prep. Weather HMM with 3, 1: 0.32/0.02, then H 0.0384, C 0.064 → H C. Cost O(N²T). HMM limits: unknown words, no rich features, limited context, sparsity, one direction. MEMMs model P(tᵢ | wᵢ, tᵢ₋₁, features) with softmax (2.0/0.5 → 0.82/0.18), decode with Viterbi (greedy can fail: the old man the boats), and suffer label bias, fixed by CRFs.
